newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Privatised Ivorian telecoms firm gets 7yr monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Privatised Ivorian telecoms firm gets 7yr monopoly.

text.p: Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie has signed a decree giving the new owners of the privatised state telecommunications firm CI-TELCOM a seven-year monopoly on the West African nation's telephone network.

A government statement, read on state television after a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, said the measure was designed to ensure the success of the privatised company in which a consortium led by France Telecom has a 51 percent stake.
"This concession is valid for 20 years with an exclusive period of seven years for exclusive services," the statement said.

Privatisation of CI-TELCOM was the jewel in the crown of the West African nation's privatisation programme. A total of 37 of the 60 companies earmarked for privatisation has been sold party or in full to the prvate sector.
Ivory Coast has been privatising state companies as part of reforms designed to liberalise its economy as sponsored by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
